notes: ACCESS: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only generic User-agent:* and Pinterestbot groups) so a full Rule 2 sweep was run. curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_0 succeeded on the first two requests (homepage 149798 bytes with full mega-menu HTML, then /c/chandeliers/ 463975 bytes with live results count) -- both used to build the category taxonomy below. Immediately after, Akamai Bot Manager (CPR_Block soft-block on most paths, a JS behavioral 'sensor' challenge on others) locked out all further requests to any /c/* listing page for the rest of the session (~40+ min of retries). Exhausted per Rule 2: direct fetch, curl_cffi across 15+ TLS profiles (chrome99-131, edge101, safari15_5-18_0/17_2_ios, firefox133/135) both bursted and slow-spaced (75-90s gaps), plain requests, PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest (same egress IP, same block), WebFetch (blocked from Anthropic infra too), r.jina.ai (its own Cloudflare challenge), translate.goog (403), and generic proxies allorigins.win/corsproxy.io/textise.net/api.codetabs.com/translated.turbopages.org (all blocked or 403/522). IPv6 anycast pinning not applicable -- www.lampsplus.com has no AAAA record (Akamai edge IPv4-only). Root-level static sitemaps (robots.txt, sitemap-index.xml, sitemap-category.xml) stayed reachable throughout and independently confirmed the category list (cross-checked against the live mega-menu), but the per-category product sitemaps under /products/*.xml that would have given exact counts are behind the same bot-manager protection as the catalog pages. Wayback Machine snapshots were checked as a last resort but most captured the same maintenance/CPR_Block page (the block appears to affect Wayback's crawler IPs too at times), so it added nothing trustworthy; two clean historical snapshots did surface (close-to-ceiling-lights 20,676 results; table-lamps 11,259 results) but per Rule 2 these are STRUCTURE-ONLY and not used as qty (not entered as rows' qty; noted here only). COUNT METHOD (Chandeliers, the only verified row): the live page showed 'Chandeliers 18,926 results' and the pagination footer '1 - 48 of 18,926 results' with a 208-page pager; fetching page 1 and page 208 both showed the identical total (18,926) with 48 distinct SKUs/product names on each (checked for duplicate-SKU inflation per Rule 1 -- names were genuinely distinct products, not color/variant records), so this is treated as a trustworthy site-reported total, not a raw platform API count. SCOPE DECISIONS: site organizes lighting primarily by fixture type (Chandeliers, Track Lighting, Pendants, Flush Mounts, Recessed, Table Lamps, Floor Lamps, Outdoor Lighting, Sconces, Picture Lights, Under Cabinet Lights, Bathroom (vanity) Lighting -- kept in scope per Rule 0 despite the room word, Wall Lamps, Wall Lights, Lamp Shades, Night Lights, Up Lights & Clip Lights, Grow Lights, Party Lights) with style_/location_/usage_/feature_/manufacturer_ URL segments nested under each as pure attribute facets of the SAME product (e.g. chandeliers/style_farmhouse, floor-lamps/type_arc-lamps) -- these were NOT extracted as separate rows since they are subsets already counted in the parent total, consistent with Rule 1's caution on fragmenting a single search index. Mirrors was treated the same way (type_vanity-mirrors / type_wall-mirrors are nested facets of the same '/c/mirrors/' listing) so Mirrors is a single childless leaf. By contrast, 'Home Accessories' (site's own umbrella/catch-all decor bucket, not a specific product type) was NOT extracted as its own leaf; instead its type_ facets that are genuinely different product forms (clocks/vases/candleholders/sculptures/wall-art) were extracted as siblings under a new 'Decor' parent, since a clock and a vase share no product identity the way 'Modern Chandelier' and 'Farmhouse Chandelier' do. Excluded from Home Accessories: type_bedding, type_throw-pillows, type_decorative-pillows (all textiles), type_electric-fireplaces (appliance/furniture-adjacent), type_pets, type_bird-houses-and-feeders (garden, not classic decor). 'Ceiling Medallions' (home-accessories/type_ceiling-medallions, found via sitemap-category.xml) kept in as a purely ornamental decorative accessory. 'Outdoor Decor' (a distinct product-sitemap segment, separate from outdoor-lighting/outdoor-furniture/outdoor-tables) kept in as likely planters/garden decorative accents per the explicit in-scope instruction that Outdoor is not a blanket exclusion; could not verify contents live. '/c/accessories/' ('Lighting Accessories') was EXCLUDED, not flagged: at a lighting specialist this section is almost always harps/finials/sockets/dimmers/remotes (functional lamp hardware), matching the explicit hardware/DIY exclusion; could not verify titles live to confirm. Sitewide room facets '/c/location_bedroom/', '/c/location_living-room/', etc. (bare URLs, not namespaced under lighting) were found in the nav/sitemap but DELIBERATELY OMITTED rather than emitted as a 'Lighting by Room' branch: their bare (non-lighting-prefixed) URL pattern strongly suggests they are sitewide mixed-department facets (spanning furniture, rugs and lighting for that room) rather than a lighting-only room tree, and Rule 0's room-tree mandate presumes the branch is genuinely lighting; this is an inference made without page access and should be manually re-verified once the site is reachable -- if it proves to be a genuine lighting-only room tree it should be added. Excluded outright (confirmed via sitemap-index.xml segment names): furniture (cabinets-and-storage, beds, seating, tables, outdoor-furniture, outdoor-tables), ceiling-fans, desk-fans-and-floor-fans, bathroom-exhaust-fans (all fans), light-bulbs, rugs, bathroom-hardware, hardware, dimmers, indoor-air-purifiers, grow-lights kept in (see below). Two borderline fixture categories (Grow Lights, Party Lights) were kept in per Rule 0 ('judge product type') since both are literally lighting fixtures rather than tools/holiday items, but flagged for manual confirmation. No duplicate-company signal found. DUPLICATE-COMPANY: none found/applicable.
